findings.claim: The exclusion glob '!components/ui-radix-backup/**' is anchored to the repo root and therefore never matches the actual backup path 'frontend/src/components/ui-radix-backup/**', so the Radix-import check does not exclude what it claims to exclude.
findings.evidence: The script cd's to the repo root (line 5) and runs `rg -l '@radix-ui/' frontend/src --glob '!components/ui-radix-backup/**'`. ripgrep override globs containing a slash are matched gitignore-style relative to the invocation root (repo root here), so the pattern only matches a top-level 'components/ui-radix-backup/' directory. The real backup lives under 'frontend/src/components/ui-radix-backup/' per tasks.md Task 1 and Task 6 ('ui-radix-backup/ → expected (backup files still import Radix)'). If the backup still exists, the gate fails spuriously, contradicting verification.md's PASS verdict; if it was deleted, the glob is dead code masking the fact that the check's stated scope is wrong.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a non-anchored pattern such as --glob '!**/ui-radix-backup/**', and assert the intended scope explicitly (e.g., test whether the backup directory exists and document which behavior is expected).

findings.claim: verification.md permanently records 'Current repository HEAD: a91cd5b...' and git hash-object digests that are unverifiable from the packet and become false the moment this very file is committed, while the gate's runtime outputs (34 wrappers, zero Radix imports, openspec validate/status passing) are still asserted without any captured output or CI wiring.
findings.evidence: The file records HEAD a91cd5b50b9061c0ef439003142e994c46b8d013 and two hash-object values, but the commit that adds verification.md necessarily has a different HEAD, so the 'current' claim is self-refuting on landing. 'The gate reports 34 Base UI-backed wrapper files and zero direct production @radix-ui/* imports' and 'openspec validate base-ui-foundation --strict passes' remain unverifiable assertions; no workflow, lefthook, or script reference in the diff invokes verify-archive-readiness.sh, so nothing ensures the gate ever runs. This is the residual of the prior self-attestation blocker: the mechanism now exists, but its execution and results are still certified only by the same change that authors it.
findings.suggested_fix: Rephrase HEAD/digests as 'at verification time' historical data, capture the gate's actual output as a committed artifact (or wire verify-archive-readiness.sh into lefthook.yml/CI), so the PASS verdict has evidence independent of the author's assertion.

findings.claim: The gate hard-codes the Base UI wrapper count at exactly 34, a magic number that will rot silently and whose relationship to the '46 UI component files' cited in proposal.md is never explained.
findings.evidence: Line 27-28: `base_ui_wrappers="$(rg -l '@base-ui/react' frontend/src/components/ui | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"; test "$base_ui_wrappers" -eq 34`. proposal.md twice says 'all 46 UI primitive components'/'all 46 UI component files' were regenerated, while tasks.md Task 5 records 45 updated + 11 new = 56 files and verification.md says the scoped diff touched 56 primitive files. The 34/46/56 discrepancy is unreconciled anywhere in the change, and any legitimate future wrapper addition before archiving breaks the gate for the wrong reason.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the exact count with a floor (e.g., -ge 1 combined with the zero-Radix check) or document in design.md why 34 of the regenerated files import @base-ui/react while the rest legitimately do not.

findings.claim: The openspec status jq predicate passes vacuously if the CLI reports zero artifacts, since `all` over an empty stream is true.
findings.evidence: `openspec status --change base-ui-foundation --json | jq -e '.isComplete == true and ([.artifacts[].status] | all(. == "done"))'` — when `.artifacts` is empty (e.g., schema change or CLI regression), `[.artifacts[].status]` is `[]` and `all` yields true, so only `.isComplete` guards the gate. verification.md claims 'proposal, design, specs, and tasks complete', which the predicate cannot actually distinguish from an empty artifact list.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a length assertion, e.g. `.artifacts | length >= 4`, or check for the specific expected artifact names.
